1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night
It had been raining in Qingshi for three days straight. Lin Xiaoyu's older sister had gone to the capital in the spring, and ever since, the little pharmacy in town had been hers alone to look after.
After dark, she shut the doors and windows, counted the day's earnings, blew out the oil lamp, and went upstairs.
She had barely lain down when urgent knocking came from the door downstairs, followed by a man's voice: "Anyone there?"
Outside stood a young man soaked to the skin, his left arm wrapped in cloth strips seeping with blood. He gave his name as Bai Yun and said he was with the Azure Dragon Society.
"I need my wound dressed," Bai Yun said in a low voice. "I can pay. Would three thousand five hundred wen be enough?"
From inside his robe he produced a letter wrapped in oilpaper. "This letter must reach Qingfeng before the eighteenth of the fifth month."
As she bandaged him, he said with a wry smile, "If my fiancée knew I'd knocked on a girl's door in the middle of the night, she'd be jealous for sure."
Lin Xiaoyu didn't take his money. She only said, "First thing tomorrow, I'll take you up the mountain."
2: They set out at first light. Lin Xiaoyu carried a bamboo basket on her back, packed with dry rations, herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the mountain, they ran into Zhou Dashan, an old woodcutter. The old man set down his axe and lowered his voice: the evening before, three strangers had been at the town gate, asking after a wounded young man.
"Xiaoyu, take the small path," Zhou Dashan said. "The main road isn't safe." Lin Xiaoyu thanked him.
The small path was narrow and slippery. Lin Xiaoyu walked ahead, planting each step firmly. Bai Yun followed behind without a word.

By noon the rain had stopped, and the mist in the mountains slowly lifted, revealing the roofs of Qingfeng in the distance. A nun stood at the temple gate—Zhao Qiuyue, the temple's guest-receiver, in charge of welcoming visitors.
Zhao Qiuyue took the letter, looked at the red seal on the flap, and nodded. "The abbess has been waiting for this letter for 2 years."
Bai Yun said to Lin Xiaoyu, "I owe you my life." Lin Xiaoyu smiled. "Then next time you come, help me fix the roof of my apothecary." Bai Yun stayed on at the temple.
At dusk, Lin Xiaoyu went down the mountain alone. It was already dark by the time she got home. She lit the lamp and sat behind the counter for a long while.
